newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to crack down on soccer hooligans.
newsitem.headline: Poland to crack down on soccer hooligans.

text.p: Poland said on Monday it was more determined than ever to secure stiff new laws against soccer hooligans after about 60 people were injured in weekend violence.
"Changes in the penal code must take place," said Interior Ministry spokesman Ryszard Hincza, quoted by PAP news agency.
"Under current law such incidents are seen as causing little harm and detained trouble-makers are usually released after police take down their details," he said.
PAP said the ministry was working with police on a bill to ensure security at public events,
Lech Poznan fans went on a rampage in their stadium, tearing up plastic seats and hurling them at police, after their team was defeated 0-2 by Legia Warszawa on Saturday.

Police responded with water-cannon and 47 police and 10 other people were injured in the ensuing battle. Twelve people were briefly detained afterwards or sent to sobering-up stations before being released.

Michal Listkiewicz, secretary general of the Polish Soccer Association, told reporters that Lech Poznan could be fined up to 50,000 zlotys (about $18,500) and have its stadium closed for the next two matches.

"The longer hooligans enjoy impunity, the tougher and costlier will be the measures needed to restrain them," said the daily Rzeczpospolita in a commentary reflecting widespread media demands for stiffer sanctions.

PAP said the governor of the southwestern province of Wroclaw was considering closing down Slask Wroclaw stadium following violent clashes on Saturday between local fans and supporters of visiting Widzew Lodz.
